diff --git a/vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py b/vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py
index dfe7102..72f100d 100644
--- a/vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py
+++ b/vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py
@@ -45,12 +45,20 @@ def apply_penalties(logits: torch.Tensor, prompt_tokens_tensor: torch.Tensor,
                                                    vocab_size, num_seqs)
     output_bin_counts, output_mask = get_token_bin_counts_and_mask(
         output_tokens_tensor, vocab_size, num_seqs)
-    repetition_penalties = repetition_penalties.unsqueeze_(dim=1).repeat(
-        1, vocab_size)
-    logits[logits > 0] /= torch.where(prompt_mask | output_mask,
-                                      repetition_penalties, 1.0)[logits > 0]
-    logits[logits <= 0] *= torch.where(prompt_mask | output_mask,
-                                       repetition_penalties, 1.0)[logits <= 0]
+    repetition_penalties = repetition_penalties.unsqueeze_(dim=1)
+    combined_mask = prompt_mask | output_mask
+    pos_mask = logits > 0
+    # Compute the per-element repetition multiplier using broadcasting:
+    # positive logits in combined positions: multiply by 1/rep (dampen)
+    # non-positive logits in combined positions: multiply by rep (dampen)
+    # non-combined positions: multiply by 1.0 (no-op)
+    # This replaces two boolean-indexed ops and eliminates the .repeat() call.
+    rep_mult = torch.where(
+        combined_mask,
+        torch.where(pos_mask, 1.0 / repetition_penalties, repetition_penalties),
+        1.0,
+    )
+    logits.mul_(rep_mult)
     # We follow the definition in OpenAI API.
     # Refer to https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/parameter-details
     logits -= frequency_penalties.unsqueeze_(dim=1) * output_bin_counts
diff --git a/vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py b/vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py

@@ -69,29 +69,27 @@ class RejectionSampler(nn.Module):
         # to the model runner with a persistent manner for better
         # performance.
         spec_token_ids = sampling_metadata.spec_token_ids
-        max_spec_len = max(len(s) for s in spec_token_ids)
         batch_size = len(spec_token_ids)
-        draft_token_ids = torch.full((batch_size, max_spec_len),
-                                     INVALID_TOKEN_ID,
-                                     device="cpu",
-                                     dtype=torch.long)
-
-        target_token_ids = torch.full((batch_size, max_spec_len + 1),
-                                      fill_value=INVALID_TOKEN_ID,
-                                      device=logits.device,
-                                      dtype=torch.long)
-
-        # TODO: Vectorize the following loop for better performance.
-        start_loc = 0
-        for i in range(batch_size):
-            num_spec_tokens = len(spec_token_ids[i])
-            draft_token_ids[i, :num_spec_tokens] = torch.tensor(
-                spec_token_ids[i], device="cpu", dtype=torch.long)
-            end_loc = start_loc + num_spec_tokens + 1
-            # Assume greedy sampling.
-            target_token_ids[i, :num_spec_tokens + 1] = torch.argmax(
-                logits[start_loc:end_loc], dim=-1)
-            start_loc = end_loc
+        spec_lens = [len(s) for s in spec_token_ids]
+        sample_lens = [x + 1 for x in spec_lens]
+        max_spec_len = max(spec_lens)
+
+        # Vectorize draft token IDs: build CPU tensors then pad in one shot.
+        spec_tensors = [
+            torch.tensor(s, device="cpu", dtype=torch.long)
+            for s in spec_token_ids
+        ]
+        draft_token_ids = pad_sequence(spec_tensors,
+                                       batch_first=True,
+                                       padding_value=INVALID_TOKEN_ID)
+
+        # Vectorize target token IDs: single argmax across all tokens, then
+        # split by sequence lengths and pad — replaces the per-item loop.
+        all_target_ids = logits.argmax(dim=-1)
+        split_targets = list(all_target_ids.split(sample_lens))
+        target_token_ids = pad_sequence(split_targets,
+                                        batch_first=True,
+                                        padding_value=INVALID_TOKEN_ID)
 
         vocab_size = logits.size(-1)
         # NOTE: CPU <-> GPU synchronization happens here.
diff --git a/vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py b/vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py
index ec6374d..6f33e0c 100644
--- a/vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py
+++ b/vllm/v1/sample/sampler.py
@@ -219,11 +219,26 @@ class Sampler(nn.Module):
         logits: torch.Tensor,
         sampling_metadata: SamplingMetadata,
     ) -> torch.Tensor:
-        # TODO(houseroad): this implementation is extremely inefficient.
-        # One idea is implement this as a PyTorch C++ op, and we may
-        # even optimize the logit_bias layout.
-        for i, logit_bias in enumerate(sampling_metadata.logit_bias):
+        logit_bias_list = sampling_metadata.logit_bias
+        if not any(logit_bias_list):
+            return logits
+        # Collect all (batch_idx, token_id, bias) entries and apply them in a
+        # single index_put_ call instead of per-element GPU kernel launches.
+        batch_indices = []
+        token_indices = []
+        bias_values = []
+        for i, logit_bias in enumerate(logit_bias_list):
             if logit_bias:
                 for token_id, bias in logit_bias.items():
-                    logits[i, token_id] += bias
+                    batch_indices.append(i)
+                    token_indices.append(token_id)
+                    bias_values.append(bias)
+        if batch_indices:
+            rows = torch.tensor(batch_indices, dtype=torch.long,
+                                device=logits.device)
+            cols = torch.tensor(token_indices, dtype=torch.long,
+                                device=logits.device)
+            vals = torch.tensor(bias_values, dtype=logits.dtype,
+                                device=logits.device)
+            logits.index_put_((rows, cols), vals, accumulate=True)
         return logits
